title: Adoption
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Adoption is God’s gracious act of receiving believers as His children through Jesus Christ. Those who were once alienated are brought into God’s family with belonging, access, inheritance, and fatherly care.
summary: Adoption is God’s gracious act of receiving believers as His children through Jesus Christ. Those who were once alienated are brought into God’s family with belonging, access, inheritance, and fatherly care.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Son through whom believers become children of God. In Him, they receive the Spirit of adoption and may cry out to God as Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Adoption shows that salvation is not only legal pardon but family belonging. God does not merely declare believers forgiven and leave them at a distance; He receives them as His children.

This adoption comes through Christ. The eternal Son became man so that sinners might receive the status and inheritance of sons. Believers belong to God because they are united to His beloved Son.

The Spirit confirms this family relationship by leading believers to cry, “Abba, Father.” Adoption gives access, assurance, discipline, comfort, and hope of inheritance.

Adoption also creates a new family identity. Believers are brothers and sisters in Christ, called to love one another as members of God’s household.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people carry father wounds, rejection, abandonment, or a sense that they do not belong anywhere. Adoption declares that in Christ, God receives His people with covenant love and gives them a family name.

This doctrine also humbles spiritual pride. No believer is a child of God by natural entitlement, status, or performance. Adoption is grace through Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as a child of God in Christ. Bring fear, shame, and rejection to your Father rather than living like an orphan. Receive His discipline, trust His care, love His family, and remember that your inheritance rests on Christ, not on your worthiness.
